modes.heading: MODES
modes.intro: Kanal runs two stages — speech into text, then text into the other languages — and each one can run on this laptop or off it. A mode picks both at once. In every mode the finished captions reach the phones through the relay, as text. Modes that cannot run yet stay in the list with the reason.
mode.demo.name: Demo — scripted
mode.demo.help: A fixed script of six utterances, looping. No microphone, no account, no key — only the scripted captions go out, so the room's screens, the join QR and the phones can be checked before anyone arrives.
mode.cloudcloud.name: Cloud transcription · Cloud translation
mode.cloudcloud.help: Both stages run off this machine in one streaming session — the lowest-latency pairing today, and the one that sends the room's audio out. Needs an API key.
mode.cloudlocal.name: Cloud transcription · Local translation
mode.cloudlocal.help: Speech is transcribed off this machine; the transcript is then translated here by a downloaded model, so no text is sent out for translation — the audio still is. Needs an API key and a translation model.
mode.localcloud.name: Local transcription · Cloud translation
mode.localcloud.help: Speech never leaves the room — only the transcript is sent out to be translated, so every network hop is text. The pairing this tool was built to reach. Waiting on local transcription.
mode.locallocal.name: Local transcription · Local translation
mode.locallocal.help: Both stages run on this laptop: the pipeline sends nothing out, and only the captions cross the network on their way to the phones. The heaviest mode on the machine. Waiting on local transcription.

empty.body2: The mode picks both stages — where speech is transcribed and where it is translated — and says what leaves this machine. Demo needs no key. A join QR appears on the right; everyone else reads on their own phone, in their own language.

settings.input.heading: INPUT
settings.input.title: Test a microphone
settings.input.note: Kanal applies no noise suppression, echo cancellation or automatic gain of its own. Whatever the microphone and the operating system do to the signal happens before Kanal sees it, and is configured per device in {0} — this test measures the result.
mic.untested.detail: Start the test and speak from where people will actually sit.
mic.listening.detail: Speak from where people will actually sit, then leave a few seconds of quiet.
mic.nobackend.detail: This platform has no capture support built in yet.
mic.silent.detail: Check that this is the right device and that Windows has not muted or disabled it.
mic.silent.detail.mac: Check that this is the right device, that its input level in System Settings → Sound is not zero, and that this app is allowed the microphone under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone — a denied permission delivers exactly this silence.
mic.quiet.detail: Raise the input level in {0}, or put the microphone nearer the table.
mic.clipping.detail: Lower the input level in {0}. A clipped consonant is gone for good — no transcriber recovers it.
mic.noisy: The room is nearly as loud as the speaker
mic.noisy.detail: Speech is only {0} dB above the room. Move the microphone closer to the talkers, or turn off whatever is making the noise.
mic.good.detail: Speech sits {0} dB above the room.
mic.good.silentroom: Speech peaks at {0} dB and the gaps are completely silent — either a very quiet room, or the device is gating the signal.
mic.readout: peak {0} dB · room {1} dB · margin {2} dB
